proposedMechanism: Resolve actual operative law at the relevant level and actual covered processing activity. Unknown legal scope remains unknown.
Match the law's specific obligation to recorded firm task units and completed work; do not create customer counts, data intensity or hours.

For incremental paid work, derive actual cost from completed units × matched sourced effort × recorded compensation, or read a completed provider invoice. Existing payroll work is an allocation/opportunity cost unless it causes a recorded new expense.
Carry lawEffectStamps and actual workload/work/payment source IDs onto the saved consequence.
Keep cash/debt writers single-entry: annotate an already posted payment rather than debit it again.

On prospective repeal remove future obligations only as the law actually permits; retain sunk implementation expense and historical records. Current retained records can still generate lawful deletion/retention tasks.
Capacity limits arise from recorded qualified worker hours/provider capacity, due dates and queue; no invented saturation or reversal curve.
Check the aggregate incremental-production-cost ratio against0.1–0.6% using the study-matched denominator and exposed firms. Never clamp, draw or force each firm/place into that interval.
unknownHandling: Missing workload/unit-cost records yield an explicit unavailable estimate, never numerical zero or an invented invoice. Current original reader/cash writer remain unchanged by this design; no repaired runtime claim.
